title: Reading schedules for book clubs
body: A club's owner can now set how many chapters a week the club reads. Everyone sees this week's chapters on the club's page, and whether they're on track, ahead or behind.

title: Export your notes as a PDF
body: My Library → Notes now saves a book's highlights, notes and journal, or all of them, as a tidy PDF as well as Markdown and plain text: chapters in order, each quote marked, with its page and your note. It's made on your device.

title: Theme challenges for the household
body: Goals → Start a challenge can now count Themes covered: nine prompts such as a book from before 1900, a book in another language, poetry or a true story. Each finished book ticks the themes it fits, and the challenge shows who covered which.

title: Bedtime in the Kids reading report
body: Account → Family and the Monday email now show, for each Kids profile with a bedtime, how many nights of the last week it was kept, and how long it spent in Bedtime listening.

title: A speed for each book
body: In Player settings, Keep this speed for this book remembers how fast you like one audiobook, on every device, while your other books keep your usual speed.

title: Character voices know who's talking
body: Character voices now follow two people talking in turn, even where only "he said" is written, and find speakers named in French, German and Spanish books as well as English ones.

title: Character voices for your uploads
body: Turn on Character voices in Player settings and a natural voice reading your upload hands what the characters say to other voices. Anyone named beside their words, as in "said Elizabeth", keeps the same voice all book long. Chapters with no speech are read as before.

title: Upload PDFs and Kindle books
body: My Library → Uploads now takes PDFs and DRM-free Kindle books (MOBI and AZW3) as well as EPUBs. They're read on your device and kept as text, like EPUBs, so you can search them, read them anywhere, listen with any voice and read them in a club. A PDF is split into parts at its bookmarks, or every 20 pages; scanned pages have no text to read.

title: Bedtime listening
body: A dim, quiet way to listen before sleep, in the player and the mini-player's More: it sets the sleep timer for you (the end of the chapter when that's near, otherwise 15 minutes), the sound fades out at the end, and Dimmer darkens the screen further. Kids profiles with a bedtime are offered it in the player shortly before. The end-of-chapter sleep timer now fades out everywhere, like the minutes one.

title: Gift cards
body: On Gifts you can now give a gift card as well as a membership: $25, $50 or $100 of credit for any plan, paid once. Pass the code on or have us email it, now or on a later day; when it's redeemed in Account, the credit comes off the person's next charges, whichever plan they choose.

title: Before you cancel
body: Cancelling in Account → Plan and billing now asks why you're leaving, if you'd like to say, and suggests something that might help instead: pausing on monthly billing, a smaller plan, your own uploads, the Help Center, or once per account a month's credit if you stay. You can always cancel anyway, and the 48-hour rule and no-refunds policy don't change.

title: A new price for Premium
body: From today, Premium is $60.00 a month ($600.00 a year; paying yearly still gets two months free). It keeps up to 12 profiles, unlimited audiobooks, 24 offline devices and up to 12 hours a month of Google's Chirp 3 HD voices for your uploads. Basic ($30.00) and Standard ($40.00) are unchanged. If you're already a member, your price stays as it is.

title: Natural voices in 17 languages
body: Natural voices for your uploads now also read Japanese, Chinese (Mandarin), Korean, Hindi, Arabic, Polish, Russian, Turkish, Swedish, Ukrainian and Tagalog books in their own language, as well as French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and Dutch. The player finds a book's language in its EPUB when you upload it.

title: Try LiteraryWorm free for 7 days
body: Your first membership now starts with 7 days free, on any plan. You add a card at checkout, but nothing is charged until the week ends, and if you cancel in Account before then you won't be charged at all. Account shows when your free week ends.

title: Natural voices: more languages, offline and in step
body: Natural voices for your uploads now read French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and Dutch books in their own language. Account → This month shows how much of your natural-voice reading is left, and the bell tells you when most is used. Parts you've played stay on your device to listen offline, the next chapter is voiced ahead on Wi-Fi, and the read-along follows each sentence.

title: New prices
body: From today, Basic is $30.00 a month ($300.00 a year), Standard $40.00 ($400.00) and Premium $50.00 ($500.00); paying yearly still gets two months free. Every plan keeps its profiles, listening hours, offline devices and natural-voice hours for your uploads, and Premium has up to 12 hours a month of Google's Chirp 3 HD voices. If you're already a member, your price stays as it is.

title: Natural voices for your uploads
body: Members can now have their uploaded books read aloud by a natural-sounding voice from Google: in the player, open Voice and choose one of six natural voices, British, American or Australian. Each part of the book is voiced the first time you play it and kept with your upload, so listening again is free. Each plan includes some new natural-voice reading a month (Basic 2 hours, Standard 6, Premium 12). Not on Kids profiles.

title: Listen to the books you upload
body: Your uploaded EPUBs can now be listened to as well as read: choose Listen in My Library → Uploads or on the book's page, and one of your device's voices reads it in the player, with your place, speed, sleep timer and bookmarks. When LiteraryWorm has the same public-domain book with a LibriVox recording, your upload offers that too, read by a person: choose Listen to their recording. The demo's uploads include the opening of Frankenstein to show it.

title: More books to read along with
body: Five more classics now show the book's own words as the LibriVox recording plays, each sentence marked as it's read: Through the Looking-Glass, A Christmas Carol, The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde and The Call of the Wild. That makes eight, with Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, Frankenstein and Pride and Prejudice. The demo also has a reminder set for a sample upcoming book, so you can see how Remind me works.

title: A fuller demo
body: The demo household now shows more of what members get: Avery has two lists and highlights in Pride and Prejudice, Avery and Sam follow a sample reader and see her newest logs, and Sam and Mia follow an author each. A Kids profile's Readers page now says plainly that Kids profiles don't follow readers.

title: Search in the menu when you're logged in
body: The header menu now has Search between Discover and My Library when you're logged in, so the full Search page, with its filters and genres, is a click away, as it already was on a phone. The header also fits better on smaller laptop screens.

title: Fuller genre pages and described covers
body: When a genre's page comes back with only a few books, the next page now loads straight away, so you aren't left with two books and a button. Book covers now tell screen readers which book they show, and the FAQ answers which genres you can browse.

title: Genres that fit better
body: Genres such as Pets, Cooking and House & Home now show only books filed under that subject, so a novel that just has the word in its title no longer turns up there. This applies when you browse a genre and when you narrow a search to one.

title: Every Google Books genre
body: Home and Search now have 64 genres to browse and filter by: besides Fantasy, Mystery, Romance and the rest, every subject Google Books files books under, from Antiques & Collectibles, Cooking and Comics & Graphic Novels to Philosophy, Travel and True Crime, with none repeated. On a phone, Home's genres are one row you swipe along. Kids profiles see the genres with books chosen for them.

title: Two new questions in the FAQ
body: The FAQ on Home and Plans now answers whether you can read along while you listen, and how to earn credit by recommending LiteraryWorm through the affiliate program.

title: Search filters scroll on a computer
body: On Search, the Filters beside the results now scroll on their own when they're taller than your window, so Length and Sort by are always within reach.

title: Read along with the real recording
body: For Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, Frankenstein and Pride and Prejudice, the player's transcript now shows the book's own words while the LibriVox recording plays, each sentence marked as it's read. We lined each recording up with the text once, ahead of time; nothing about your listening is sent anywhere.

title: An age check for books marked mature
body: Before a grown-up's profile, or a visitor, opens a book that Google Books or Open Library marks as mature, LiteraryWorm now asks you to confirm you're 18 or older. A profile is asked once, on every device; a visitor once a visit. Kids and Teen profiles still can't open these books at all.

title: The affiliate program
body: Recommend LiteraryWorm and earn credit: members can apply on the new Affiliate program page in the footer. Once you're approved, you get your own sign-up link, and when someone joins with it and makes their first payment, 20% of that payment is added to your membership as credit. You see visits, sign-ups and credit earned, never who signed up. Affiliates say they earn a commission wherever they share, and never aim it at children.

title: More books on Home, from Open Library
body: On a grown-up's profile, Home's genre rows and Keep discovering now come from Open Library, the free catalogue run by the Internet Archive, with Google Books stepping in when it has nothing. You'll see different books and editions, with Details from Open Library on their pages. Teen profiles, search and the public home page still use Google Books.

title: Keep discovering stays quick, with Back to top
body: Members' Keep discovering on Home now says which genre it has reached as it runs on from one to the next, and once it's long it offers Back to top of the feed. Books far off the screen aren't drawn until you come near them, so a long scroll stays smooth on older phones.

title: Accessibility settings follow your profile
body: The accessibility menu now remembers your choices for each profile: text size, theme, Lexend or OpenDyslexic, high contrast, underlined links, stopped animations and the read-along transcript's settings. A member's profile opens with them on every device, so you set them once.

title: Keep scrolling on Home, and OpenDyslexic for the whole app
body: Keep discovering on Home no longer stops at the end of a genre: it runs on into the next one, through every genre, for as long as you scroll. Visitors to the public home page see a sample of books first, then can log in, join or try the demo to keep going. The accessibility menu has a new OpenDyslexic switch that sets the whole app in OpenDyslexic (choosing it turns Lexend off, and the other way round), and the menu now scrolls inside the window, so its last settings are never cut off on a smaller screen.

title: Books load faster, from our own copy
body: When Google Books tells us about a book or a list, we now keep the answer for a short while, cover link included, so the next person to open it gets it straight away. Each answer is kept only as long as Google allows, never more than a week, and then asked for again, so new editions and changes come through. Nothing about you is kept with them.

title: The demo shows the newest features
body: Try the demo now has a sample invite link in Account → Plan and billing, last night's reading sprint in Goals and on the demo club's page, and Jordan's wishlist, which opens Gifts with its five books picked. Carmilla and The Picture of Dorian Gray are now among the LGBTQIA+ books.

title: LGBTQIA+ books to browse and search
body: LGBTQIA+ is now a genre on Home's Keep discovering, Discover, Search's Or browse a genre and the genre filter, and among the favourite genres for a profile. Its books come from Google Books, which files them under LGBTQ+; like every list, titles Google marks as mature are left out.

title: Home tells you when a sprint is on
body: When someone at home starts a reading sprint, Home shows the time left and takes you to Goals to join in. The home page, Plans and the FAQs now describe reading sprints, gift wishlists, inviting friends and the app in seven languages.

title: Gift wishlists
body: Every list you share by link is now a wishlist too. Its page has Give this list as a gift, which opens Gifts with up to 10 of its LiteraryWorm books already picked, so family and friends can give you a membership that comes with the books you want.

title: Invite a friend, both get a month free
body: Share your link from Account → Plan and billing. When a friend joins with it and makes their first payment, you each get a month of your own plan free, taken off your next bill. You can earn up to 2 free months this way, and every friend you invite still gets theirs.

title: Reading sprints
body: Start a 15 to 30 minute reading sprint from Goals for everyone at home, or from a book club's page for its members. Everyone sees the same timer, the reader shows the time left and your pages as you go, and when it ends you see how many pages each of you turned. Kids profiles can join sprints at home.

title: LiteraryWorm in seven languages
body: Choose Español, Français, Deutsch, Português, Italiano or Nederlands in the accessibility menu, and the whole app follows: menus, buttons, messages, the reader and player, car mode, My Library, Account, clubs and the plan FAQ. A visit starts in your browser's language. Dates and billing days follow the language too. Books stay in the language they were written in, the policies stay in English with a note in your language, and voice control in car mode still listens for English words.

title: Stronger high contrast
body: High contrast in the accessibility menu now turns the app black or white, with every text colour at the WCAG AAA level, stronger edges on buttons and fields, and underlined links. It's on from the start when your device asks for more contrast, and Windows contrast themes keep every button, switch and progress bar visible.

title: Vote on your book club's next read
body: A club's owner can ask What to read next on the club's page: offer two to five LiteraryWorm books and members vote, seeing everyone's votes and changing theirs until the poll closes. The book with the most votes wins, and Start a club with it begins a club for it in one step. New polls show in the bell.

title: Voice control in car mode
body: In car mode, turn on Voice control and say Play, Pause, Back, Forward, Next chapter, Previous chapter or Exit car mode, with a length if you like (“back 30 seconds”). It's off until you turn it on, listens only while car mode is open and on screen, and your browser's own speech service hears the words; LiteraryWorm keeps nothing. Not on Kids profiles.

title: Discussion questions for book clubs
body: On a book club's page for a public-domain classic, Discussion questions gives five to eight questions about a chapter you've reached, written by AI from the book up to the end of that chapter only, so nothing later is given away. Choose Start a post with this to begin a post with one. Every club at that chapter gets the same questions.

title: Bigger car mode buttons on phones and tablets
body: On phones and tablets, in the browser or the installed app, online or offline, car mode now fills the screen with bigger buttons, icons and words. Held upright, Back and Forward are on the first row, Play goes across the middle, and Previous and Next chapter are below. A tablet on its side has two rows with Play down the middle, and a phone on its side has all five in one tall row.

title: Car mode looks the same on phones and in the app
body: On a phone, and in the installed app, car mode now has the same buttons in the same order as on a bigger screen: Back, Play and Forward side by side with Play in the middle, and Previous and Next chapter under them. With the phone on its side in a dashboard mount, everything fits on one screen.

title: More ways to sort when starting a club
body: When you start a club, Sort by has the same eleven choices as My Library for LiteraryWorm books and your uploads: recently added, oldest added, recently changed, title, numbers first, author, published year and series in reading order. For LiteraryWorm books, the date sorts put the books in your library first.

title: Sort My Library by series
body: My Library's Sort by has Series, in reading order: each series comes together, A to Z, with its books in order, then the books in no series by title. LiteraryWorm books use their series, and other books the one their title names, such as "(The Expanse, #1)". Uploads sort the same way.

title: Sort your uploads eleven ways
body: My Library → Uploads has Sort by under the search box: Recently added, Oldest added, Recently changed (the last time you read it), Title A–Z or Z–A, Numbers first, Author A–Z or Z–A, Published newest or oldest, and Series in reading order. The published year comes from the EPUB itself, so books uploaded before today sort last by it, and the series is the one a title names, such as "(The Expanse, #1)".

title: Counting visits with Ahrefs Web Analytics
body: If you allow analytics in the consent banner, Ahrefs Web Analytics counts the pages people visit, so we can see what's used. It sets no cookies, page addresses go without search words or codes, and it never runs for Kids profiles or on pages with codes in their links. The Privacy Policy, Cookie Policy, Children's Privacy Notice and Your Privacy Choices say so.

title: Keyword searches to try on Discover and Search
body: Discover and Search's start suggest a few keyword searches, such as Detective, Ghost and Friendship. Each looks through descriptions, genres and series as well as titles and authors. The Plans cards and the home page now say you can search your uploads by title, author, keywords or ISBN, even inside their text.

title: Find uploads by ISBN, and club books by keywords
body: My Library → Uploads can now search your EPUBs by ISBN too: Google Books says which book it is, and your uploads with that title and author show. When you start a club, Find a book and Find one of your uploads take a title, author, keywords or ISBN in one box: keywords also look through LiteraryWorm books' descriptions and genres, and your uploads' part names.

title: Search by keywords, and search your uploads
body: Search has a new choice, Keywords: it finds books with every word you type anywhere in the title, author, narrator, description, genres or series, with the same filters as a title search. It's in the header's search box too. In My Library → Uploads you can now search your own EPUBs by title, author or keywords; keywords look through the books' text on your device and link to each page where the words are.

title: A clearer Cookie Policy and Privacy Policy
body: The Cookie Policy starts with In short and a list of everything your browser keeps for LiteraryWorm, who sets it and how long it stays, and says what loads from other sites, such as Google Fonts and Stripe's checkout page. The Privacy Policy says what we don't do, how we keep your information safe, and how long we keep each kind of it.

title: Clearer policies and Help
body: Your Privacy Choices, the Return Policy, the Terms of Service, the End User License Agreement, the Acceptable Use Policy, the Disclaimer, Copyright/DMCA, the Accessibility Policy and the Children's Privacy Notice are easier to read, most with an In short summary at the top, and up to date with content notes, Translate, audio clips and buddy reads. Help is grouped by topic: reading and listening, your library, profiles and family, book clubs, your plan, and logging in.

title: Google Books cookies, said plainly
body: Because LiteraryWorm uses the Google Books API, covers of books from Google Books, and the Google Books preview on some book pages, load from books.google.com, and Google sets its own third-party cookies on our website when they do. The Cookie Policy, Privacy Policy, Help, the FAQ and the Children's Privacy Notice now say so, and how to block them; Kids profiles don't load Google Books.

title: Feel-good picks on Discover, and moods on Search
body: Discover now has a Feel-good picks row of the books you tagged funny, hopeful, lighthearted, relaxing or inspiring, to read again. Search lists the moods you've used, each opening those books in My Library, and reminds you that Translate works in any classic.

title: Better search results
body: LiteraryWorm now tells search engines more, and more accurately: each LiteraryWorm title's page describes the book, its ebook and its LibriVox audiobook; Plans and the home page describe the membership, each plan's monthly and yearly price, and the questions about plans; and every page names LiteraryWorm, its support address and its search.

title: Buddy reads
body: Read a book with one friend: choose Read with a friend on any LiteraryWorm title's page and a buddy read starts straight away, with an invite code to send them. It's a book club for two, with spoiler-safe posts by chapter, meetings, shared highlights and where you each are, and it takes your friend and no one else.

title: Content notes
body: Every LiteraryWorm title's page now has Content notes: how much violence, death, frightening scenes, language, sexual content, alcohol and drugs, prejudice, and self-harm a book has (none, mild, moderate or strong), each with a short note and no spoilers, and a line on who it suits. Grown-ups see them under a Kids profile's book requests in Account → Family too. They're written by AI from the book's details, the same for everyone, and nothing about you is sent.

title: Share a clip of an audiobook
body: In the player, or the mini-player's More menu, choose Share a clip to share the last 15, 30 or 60 seconds you heard of a LibriVox recording as a link. Anyone can open it and play that stretch, with the book and narrator named. The recordings are in the public domain, and nothing is recorded or uploaded: the clip page plays it straight from the Internet Archive.

title: Translate a passage
body: In the classics, select some words and choose Translate to read them in English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese or Dutch. It's handy for the French, German and Spanish classics, and works in every public-domain title. The translation is written by AI, and only the words you selected are sent. Not on Kids profiles.

title: Bedtime for Kids profiles
body: Grown-ups can now set a bedtime for a Kids profile in its profile editor, from 7pm to 10pm, and when reading starts again in the morning. From bedtime until then, books and audiobooks show Time for bed, on that device's clock, and the place is saved. The account password allows 15 more minutes.

title: Moods and pace
body: Tag how a book felt on its page, under How did it feel?: up to three moods, such as funny, hopeful, dark or tense, and a pace (slow, medium or fast). Each profile keeps its own. My Library can show only the books with one mood, the Feel-good picks smart list gathers the cheerful ones, and the StoryGraph export carries your moods and pace.

title: A clearer Children's Privacy Notice
body: We rewrote the Children's Privacy Notice for parents and guardians. It now starts with a short summary, groups what a Kids profile keeps, lists what we never collect, explains the AI features a Kids profile can use (only the book's own text reaches Anthropic), says who can see a child's reading and for how long it's kept, and how to withdraw consent or ask us a question.

title: Didn't finish, and reading a book again
body: Your library has a fourth status, Didn't finish, for books you put down; it has its own tab in My Library, and recommendations stop pushing books like it. A finished book now has Read again on its page: it goes back to Reading from the start, and finishing it again counts as another read, so the page says "Your 2nd read" or "Read twice". Exports for Goodreads and StoryGraph carry both, and imports read StoryGraph's did-not-finish.

title: Find a club's book by ISBN
body: When you start a book club, Find a book and, under My uploads, Find one of your uploads also take an ISBN (10 or 13 digits, with or without dashes), and so does Find your copy on a club's page. We look it up on Google Books and show the LiteraryWorm title or your uploaded EPUB with that title and author.

title: Sort and filter books when starting a club
body: When you start a book club, the Book list can be sorted by title (A–Z or Z–A), author, numbers first or series in reading order, and filtered to one series or to books in none. It works for LiteraryWorm titles and for your uploaded DRM-free EPUBs, including ones you bought; an upload's series comes from its title, such as "(The Expanse, #1)".

title: Upload up to 20 books at a time
body: In My Library → Uploads you can now choose up to 20 DRM-free EPUBs at once. Each can still be up to 50 MB, and LiteraryWorm reads them one after another, then tells you which are ready and which weren't added and why.

title: 16 new badges
body: My Library → Badges now has 30 badges. New ones: 25 and 100 books, two weeks and 100 days in a row, 100 reading days, a three-hour marathon day, 50 and 250 hours, your first hour and 50 hours of listening, 10 genres, a book in another language, 25 classics, three series, 50 words and 100 highlights. They're worked out from what you already read, listen to and keep, so any you've already earned show straight away.

title: Book clubs on books you uploaded
body: Start a book club around a book you uploaded, such as a DRM-free EPUB you bought: choose My uploads when you start one, and search by title or author to find it. Your file stays private. The club sees the title and author, and each member uploads their own copy and chooses it on the club's page, so the discussion, where everyone is and shared highlights follow their place in it without spoilers.

title: New plan prices, and Standard with 3 profiles
body: Basic is now $15.00 a month ($150.00 a year), Standard $20.00 ($200.00) with up to 3 profiles, and Premium $30.00 ($300.00) with up to 12 profiles and unlimited listening. A year is still ten months' price. If you're already a member, your price stays as it is, and a Standard household that already has more than 3 profiles keeps them. Questions about plans now covers each plan's features and more about the app.

title: Help when logging in doesn't respond
body: If Log in or Log in with a passkey does nothing, check your browser's site settings: LiteraryWorm never needs access to your local network, and allowing it can stop logging in from working. Help, the log-in page, the Privacy Policy and the Cookie Policy now say how to turn it off.

title: Offline listening on a schedule
body: On an audiobook's page, Read offline now has Listen offline on a schedule: as you listen, this device keeps the chapter you're on and the next 1, 3, 5 or 10 saved, on Wi-Fi only if you like, and can remove the ones you've finished. The next part is always there for the commute, without saving the whole book.

title: OpenDyslexic, a reading ruler and line focus
body: The reader's Display settings now offer OpenDyslexic, a font made for readers with dyslexia, and a Reading guide: a ruler that marks the line you're on, or line focus, which dims everything but three lines. It follows your pointer or a tap, and J and K move it a line.

title: Export your library for Goodreads or StoryGraph
body: My Library has Export for Goodreads and Export for StoryGraph: a CSV of your books, shelves, star ratings and the days you added and finished them, in that site's own layout, ready to import there. It's made on your device; nothing is uploaded.

title: Gift a book or a list with a membership
body: When you buy a gift membership, you can add up to 10 LiteraryWorm books to it: find a title, or add one of your lists. They're named in the email if we send it, and waiting in the recipient's library when they redeem the gift.

title: Reading plans: finish by a date
body: On any book's page, choose a day to finish it by. Reading plan works out about how many minutes (at your own pace) or pages a day get you there, and tells you whether you're on track, ahead or behind. Home lists your plans with the days left. Change the date or remove a plan any time.

title: Share highlights with your book club
body: On a club's page, Shared highlights shows the passages members marked in the book, with their notes if they chose to share them. Ones from chapters you haven't reached stay hidden until you choose to see them, like posts. Share one of your own from the list there, and stop sharing it whenever you like.

title: Review your highlights
body: My Library → Notes now has Review for your highlights: each passage you marked comes back the day after, then after 1, 3, 7, 14, 30 and 60 days while it still matters, with your note and a link to the page. Up to 10 a day, and Home tells you when some are due.

title: Classics in their own language, easier to find
body: Discover has a new row, In their own language, with the classics in French, German and Spanish, and Search lists them under Or read a classic in its own language. Plans and the home page now describe notifications on your devices, Previously… recaps, your time with each book and where everyone is in a club.

title: Previously…, a recap when you come back
body: Coming back to a classic audiobook? Previously… in the player (and in the mini-player's More) catches you up from the second chapter on: the story so far and what happened last time. It's written by AI from the chapters before yours only, so nothing ahead is given away.

title: Your time with each book
body: A book's page now shows Your time with this book once you've read or listened to it: the time you've spent, reading and listening, the days, your pace through the book with the time left at that pace, and your biggest days. It's private to your profile.

title: More notifications, your choice
body: Notifications on your devices can now also tell you about a club meeting coming up, new posts in your clubs (only up to your chapter), an evening nudge to keep a reading streak, and a grown-up's answer to a Kids book request. Choose which in Account → Preferences, under Notifications on this device.

title: Classics in French, German and Spanish
body: Six classics to read and hear in their own language: Voltaire's Candide and Flaubert's Madame Bovary in French, Fontane's Effi Briest and Busch's Max und Moritz in German, and Pérez Galdós's Marianela and Lazarillo de Tormes in Spanish. Each has the full text and a LibriVox recording in that language. Find them with Search's language filter.

title: Smart lists
body: My Library has Smart lists that fill themselves: Almost there for books you're past halfway through, Waiting for you for books you started and haven't opened in a month, From authors you follow, and Loved it. They change as you read; there's nothing to keep up.

title: See where your club is
body: A book club's page now shows where everyone is in the book: each member's chapter and how far through they are, for members who turn on Show my place to this club. It's off until you choose, it shows nothing else about your reading, and posts past your chapter stay hidden as before.

title: Your year as a story
body: In My Library → Stats, Play as a story walks through your year one screen at a time: your time with books, books finished, your best streak, favourites and busiest month. Each screen is sized for Instagram, Facebook and TikTok stories, to share, download or copy. It's drawn on your device; nothing is uploaded.

title: The family shelf
body: Grown-up and teen profiles can put a book on the family shelf from its page, and it shows on Home for everyone at home. Kids profiles see the books on it that their rating allows, so a shelf of bedtime stories or holiday reading is one place for the whole household.

title: Notifications on your devices
body: Turn on Notifications on this device in Account → Preferences, and a book any profile set Remind me on tells you the day it comes out, on your phone, tablet or computer. Tap it to open the book. Turn it on for each device you like; logging out turns it off there. On iPhone and iPad, add LiteraryWorm to your Home Screen first.

title: A gentler sleep timer
body: A sleep timer set for minutes now fades the narrator out over its last 30 seconds instead of stopping mid-sentence. When it pauses the book, 15 more minutes is one tap away in the player and the mini-player, and pressing play again starts 30 seconds earlier, in case you were drifting off.

title: Passkeys skip the code
body: If you've turned on two-step sign-in, logging in with a passkey no longer asks for the code from your authenticator app: the passkey already needs your device and your face, fingerprint or screen lock. Logging in with your password still asks for the code.

title: Book rows keep loading
body: When Google Books turns our requests away for a while, LiteraryWorm now asks again another way, so the rows on Home, Search, the genre pages and author pages keep filling instead of saying they couldn't load.

title: A tour of LiteraryWorm on the home page
body: The home page now shows what LiteraryWorm does beyond reading and listening: highlights and word review, Ask the book, goals and streaks, the private journal, book clubs, listening anywhere, reading offline and following authors. It also says how Kids profiles can ask a grown-up for a book.

title: A private reading journal
body: Every book's page now has My journal: dated notes about the book that only you see, apart from the public reader logs. Write, edit and delete entries, and export them with your highlights from My Library → Notes.

title: Review your words
body: My words now asks each word again just before you'd forget it: after 1, 3, 7, 14, 30 and 60 days while you know it, and tomorrow when you don't. Home says when words are due, and Review in My words goes through them.

title: Rest days for your streak
body: Every profile gets two rest days a month. Miss a day and a rest day is used for you, so your reading streak keeps going. Goals shows how many are left this month and which days your streak rested on, and the evening reminder only comes once they're used up.

title: Kids can ask for a book
body: When a book isn't on a Kids profile's shelf, the child can tap Ask a grown-up. The request shows in the grown-ups' notifications and in Account → Family, where a grown-up says yes or no with the account password. A yes opens that one book for that profile.

title: Twelve highlight colours
body: Highlights now come in twelve colours: lime, indigo, brown and grey join yellow, green, blue, pink, orange, purple, teal and red. Pick one when you highlight, or change a highlight's colour in Notes and highlights.

title: Notices before planned updates
body: When we plan an update that might log you out or slow things down for a moment, a notice across the top of every page says when, in your own time zone. Hide it with the cross; it goes by itself when the work is done.

title: Sort My library by author Z–A
body: My library's Sort by now has Author Z–A as well as A–Z, by the author's surname.

title: Log in with a passkey
body: Add a passkey in Account → Sign-in and log in with your face, fingerprint, screen lock or a security key instead of typing your password. Give each passkey a name you'll recognise, rename it or remove it there too. Your device keeps the passkey, and your face and fingerprint never leave it. If two-step sign-in is on, you'll still enter the code from your app.

title: Sort My library
body: Sort My library by title (A–Z or Z–A), with titles that start with a number first, by author, by when you added a book or last changed it, or by when it was published. Uploads sort by the date you uploaded them. Your choice stays in the address with the Show filter.

title: Search by author or ISBN from the header
body: The search box at the top of every page now has Title, Author and ISBN (ISBN for grown-up and teen profiles, since it looks on Google Books), so you can search the way you like without opening Search first.

title: Follow other readers
body: Members can now follow other readers who share their logs. Turn on Let other readers follow me in Account → Preferences to get a reader page with the logs you publish; on a book's page, a sharing reader's name opens theirs, with Follow. Their newest logs are in My Library → Readers. Only you see who you follow, your library and reading stay private, and turning your page off removes your followers.

title: Chapter quizzes
body: In the reader of a classic, Chapter quiz asks a few questions about the chapter you're on, with the answer explained after each, for every profile, Kids included. The questions are written by AI from that chapter only, so nothing later is given away, and nothing about you is sent. Grown-ups see a Kids profile's quizzes in Account → Family.

title: Car mode and casting
body: The player has a Car mode: five big buttons, the title and the time left, and the screen kept on. Where your browser can, Cast to a speaker or TV plays a classic's recording on a Chromecast or AirPlay device. Both are in the mini-player's More menu too.

title: Up next
body: Line up audiobooks with Add to Up next on a book's page. When a book finishes, the player and the mini-player offer the next one, from your place in it. Reorder or remove them in My Library → Up next.

title: Series pages
body: Books in a series now say so (Book 2 of 6 in Anne of Green Gables) and link to the series page, with every book in reading order and where you are. Finish one and Home's Continue the series row offers the next; the end of a book names it too. 40 series to start, from Oz and Sherlock Holmes to Barsetshire.

title: My words
body: In the reader's dictionary, Keep in My words saves a word with its meaning and the sentence it came from. Find them in My Library → Words, and Practise them as flashcards: the word first, then its meaning, I knew it or Not yet.

title: Export your notes and highlights
body: Save a book's notes and highlights as Markdown or plain text from the reader's Notes and highlights, or every book's at once from My Library → Notes. The file is made on your device; nothing is uploaded.

title: Time left
body: The reader shows about how long the rest of the chapter and the book will take, at your own pace, which it learns as you read (and remembers on all your devices). The player shows the time left at your speed.

title: Badges
body: My Library → Badges shows 14 milestones, from a first finish and a week in a row to Explorer, Classic reader and Series complete, with progress towards each. A new badge shows in the bell for a week.

title: Keyboard shortcuts in the reader
body: Press ? in the reader to see its shortcuts: the arrows turn pages, C opens the chapters, N your notes, B bookmarks the page, D the dictionary and T the display settings.

title: Eight highlight colours
body: Highlights now come in eight colours: orange, purple, teal and red join yellow, green, blue and pink.

title: Search by ISBN
body: Search now has a third choice beside Title and Author: ISBN. Type the 10- or 13-digit number from the back of a book or its copyright page, with or without hyphens, to find that edition on Google Books. We check the number first, so a mistyped digit is caught straight away.

title: 300 more classics: 871 to read and hear
body: Ulysses, The Divine Comedy, Paradise Lost, Beowulf, Leaves of Grass, Pinocchio, The Blue Fairy Book, Rob Roy, Grant's memoirs, Two Years Before the Mast, The King in Yellow, Arsène Lupin, Dr Thorndyke, Henty's and Altsheler's adventures and 280 others are now in LiteraryWorm, each with the whole book to read and a LibriVox recording to listen to. That's 871 classics in all.

title: New price for Basic
body: Basic is now $9.99 a month ($99.90 a year), for new memberships and gifts. If you're already a member, your price stays as it is.

title: New prices for Standard and Premium
body: Standard is now $14.99 a month ($149.90 a year) and Premium $24.99 a month ($249.90 a year), for new memberships and gifts. Basic stays at $7.99. If you're already a member, your price stays as it is.

title: 250 more classics: 571 to read and hear
body: Trollope's Palliser and Barsetshire novels, more Scott, Hardy, Collins and Dumas, The Maltese Falcon, The Sun Also Rises, Kim, The Woman in White, Tom Swift, the Bobbsey Twins, more Tarzan, Wodehouse and 230 others are now in LiteraryWorm, each with the whole book to read and a LibriVox recording to listen to. That's 571 classics in all.

title: 250 more classics: 321 to read and hear
body: Middlemarch, David Copperfield, The Three Musketeers, Crime and Punishment, Anne of Avonlea, Tarzan of the Apes, ten more Oz books, Wodehouse, Woolf and 240 others are now in LiteraryWorm, each with the whole book to read and a LibriVox recording to listen to. That's 321 classics in all.

title: 50 more classics to read and hear
body: Emma, Great Expectations, Wuthering Heights, Huckleberry Finn, The Hound of the Baskervilles, Heidi, The War of the Worlds and 43 more classics are now in LiteraryWorm, each with the whole book to read and a LibriVox recording to listen to, chapter by chapter. That's 71 in all.

title: Book club posts by email
body: Turn on Email me new book club posts in Account → Preferences and we'll send one email a day when there's something new in your clubs: which chapters, how many posts and who wrote them. Only chapters you've reached, so no spoilers; the posts themselves stay in the app.

title: One device per browser
body: Listen on another device no longer lists the same browser twice after a refresh or in a second tab. Each browser you're signed in on is one device, and it's forgotten when you sign out.

title: Set a profile aside
body: Moving to a smaller plan? Instead of deleting a profile, set it aside in Who's reading?: it keeps its shelf, history and settings and doesn't count towards the plan. Bring it back when there's room, or it comes back by itself when you move up a plan.

title: Email a gift to someone
body: When you buy a gift membership you can now have us email the code to the person it's for, with a short message from you. A gift that starts now arrives within the hour; one for a later day arrives that morning. We forget their address once it's sent.

title: Club meetings in your calendar app
body: Each book club now has a calendar link for its members. Add it to Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Outlook once, and new, moved and cancelled meetings update by themselves.

title: Most-followed authors on Home
body: Home now shows the authors readers on LiteraryWorm follow most, with how many follow each. Follow one straight from the row.

title: Plan limits when moving to monthly at renewal
body: A yearly membership set to move to a smaller monthly plan at renewal now has that plan's room for profiles and offline devices straight away, so nothing needs removing on renewal day.

title: A reminder before a gift starts
body: Bought a gift membership for a later day? We'll email you three days before it starts, so you remember to pass the code on. The email links to your gifts; the code itself stays on the Gifts page.

title: Meeting changes update your calendar
body: When a book club meeting moves or is cancelled, the email now comes with a calendar file. Open it and the meeting moves in your calendar, or comes out of it.

title: Kids report in groups
body: The Kids reading report in Account and the Monday email now group Kids profiles: still working on their goal, no reading yet, reading without a goal, and goal reached. Handy now that a household can have up to 12 profiles.

title: Follower counts in author search
body: Searching by author now shows how many readers follow each author it finds, next to Follow.

title: Moving to a smaller plan
body: Before you move to a plan with fewer profiles or offline devices, Plans now says how many profiles to remove and devices to free, with links to do it.

title: More profiles and offline devices
body: Standard now has 5 profiles and Read offline on 10 devices (was 3 and 3), and Premium 12 profiles and 24 devices (was 5 and 5), at the same prices. Basic is unchanged.

title: Switch to yearly from the bell
body: Paying monthly for nearly a year? The bell now shows what paying yearly would save on your plan, with a link to switch.

title: Give a gift that starts later
body: When you buy a gift membership you can now choose the day it starts, up to a year ahead, so you can buy it now for a birthday. You get the code straight away, and it can be redeemed from that day.

title: A weekly goal for everyone
body: Grown-up and teen profiles can now set their own weekly reading goal in Goals, from 1 to 5 hours a week, and see how close they are over the last 7 days. Kids profiles still have theirs set by a grown-up.

title: See who follows an author
body: Author and narrator pages now show how many readers follow them, and My Library has a new Following tab listing everyone you follow, with their pages and Unfollow.

title: Change a club meeting's time
body: Club owners can now change a meeting's time, length, name or note, instead of cancelling it and adding a new one. When a meeting moves or is cancelled, everyone in the club gets an email with the old and new times, unless they turned meeting emails off.

title: Gift a year for the yearly price
body: A year's gift membership now costs the yearly price, so it comes with two months free, just like paying yearly. Gifts of 1, 3 or 6 months are still the monthly price for each month.

title: Follow authors from search
body: Searching by author now lists the authors it finds above the books, with how many of the results are theirs and a Follow button, so you can follow someone without opening their page.

title: Weekly reading goals for Kids profiles
body: Grown-ups can now give a Kids profile a weekly reading goal, from 1 to 5 hours, in the profile's settings. Kids see how close they are in Goals, grown-ups see it in Account → Family, and the Monday Kids reading report says whether the goal was reached.

title: Yearly members can switch to monthly
body: If you pay yearly, you can now choose monthly billing on the Plans page. Your year carries on as it is, and monthly billing starts on your renewal date. Changed your mind? Keep yearly billing in Account.

title: Who's coming to club meetings
body: Book club meetings now ask everyone whether they're coming: Going, Maybe or Can't make it, with who's going shown on the club page. Meetings in the next day show up in the notification bell, and if you can't make one we won't send you the reminder.

title: Book club meetings
body: Whoever started a book club can now schedule its meetings. Everyone in the club sees them on the club page, can add them to their calendar in one tap, and gets an email reminder the day before.

title: A weekly reading report for Kids profiles
body: Account → Family now shows how each Kids profile read this week: time, days read and books finished. Turn on Email me this every week to get it on Monday mornings.

title: A tidier footer
body: The links at the foot of every page are now grouped under Explore, Help, Your privacy and Legal.

title: Search by author
body: Search can now find books by who wrote them: choose Author above the search box and type any part of a name, such as tolkien or le guin. Title search works as before.

title: Goals and streaks in the bell
body: The bell now tells you when a streak of three days or more ends tonight (from 6 pm, until you read), when you're one or two books from this year's goal, and when you reach it.

title: Pay yearly, two months free
body: Every plan can now be paid yearly, at ten times the monthly price. Choose Yearly on Plans, or switch from monthly at any time: your year starts straight away, with the unused part of the month taken off. The bell reminds you 30 days before your year renews.

title: Move up a plan in one tap
body: When this month's listening or your offline devices run out, the message offers the next plan up and opens its checkout straight away.

title: A heads-up before your listening runs out
body: On Basic and Standard, the player shows how much of this month's listening is left, and the bell lets you know once the household has used most of it.

title: The New label in notifications
body: The New label on a notification now sits next to its title instead of stretching across the panel.

title: Plan limits on listening and offline devices
body: Each plan's audiobook hours and offline devices now apply: Basic 5 hours a month and 1 device, Standard 30 hours and 3 devices, Premium unlimited listening and 5 devices. Account → Plan and billing shows this month's listening and lets you free a device.

title: Favourite genres from the full list
body: Pick favourites from all nineteen genres when you set up or edit a profile. Up to two that aren't already on Home get a row of their own there, and more of our own titles are tagged Thriller, Historical Fiction and Fantasy.

title: More genres to browse and search
body: Alongside Technology, Adventure, Sci-Fi, Fiction, Non-Fiction and Horror, you can now browse and search Fantasy, Mystery, Thriller, Romance, Classics, Historical Fiction, Young Adult, Children's, Biography & Memoir, History, Science, Self-Help and Poetry.

title: What's new
body: This page: every new feature, fix and update, newest first. Turn on the monthly round-up of the biggest changes in Account → Preferences.

title: Who's who
body: In the reader of a public-domain classic, the people icon lists the characters you've met so far, with what the book has shown about them. Nobody you haven't met yet is listed, and nothing later is given away.

title: Import from Goodreads or StoryGraph
body: Bring your reading history: export it from either site and choose Import in My Library. We find each book, show you the matches, and add them with your shelves and star ratings. Books you'd already read don't count towards this year's goal.

title: Household reading challenges
body: Take on a goal together, like 5 books in November or 20 hours this month. Everyone in the household can join and see each other's progress in My Library → Goals.

title: Share your year
body: Year in Review can now be shared as a picture: your books, hours, longest streak, covers and favourite genre, in a dark or light card.

title: New books from authors you follow
body: When an author you follow has a new book out, it shows in the bell, and a weekly email lists them. Turn the email off in Account → Preferences.

title: The notification bell
body: The bell at the top counts what's new for your profile: books you set Remind me on that are out, new posts in your book clubs and new books from authors you follow. What you've seen is seen on every device.

title: Cancel at least 48 hours before your billing date
body: To stop the next charge, cancel at least 48 hours before your billing date. Cancelling later still ends your membership, after one more month. Account shows which applies before you confirm. No refunds.

title: The price after a promo code
body: Account now shows what your plan will cost once a promo code stops applying.

title: Clearer plans and more answers
body: Each plan lists everything it includes, and Common questions now covers billing, pausing, gifts, audiobooks, importing, privacy and the AI features.

title: A confirmation when you delete your account
body: After an account is deleted, we email the address to confirm what was removed and that nothing more will be charged.

title: No sideways scrolling on narrow phones
body: The header on the home page no longer pushes Sign up off the screen while the app's font is loading.

title: Invite friends to your book club by email
body: Send an invitation from the club's page; the email links straight to joining.

title: An email when a book you're waiting for comes out
body: Set Remind me on a book that isn't out yet, and we'll email you on the day as well as showing it on Home.

title: Gift memberships
body: Give one, three, six or twelve months of any plan, paid once. The code never expires.
